value: An owner may not raise the gross rent over any 12 months by more than 5 percent plus the local change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent charged in the previous 12 months; no more than two increases in 12 months; a new tenancy can start at any rent. Exempt: housing with a certificate of occupancy under 15 years old, some single-family homes and condominiums with a notice in the lease, owner-occupied duplexes and affordable housing. In force until 1 January 2030 (Civil Code 1947.12).

value: Security may not exceed one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent (two months where the landlord is a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units). Applies to security demanded on or after 1 July 2024. A lease may not call a deposit "nonrefundable" (Civil Code 1950.5(c), (n)).

value: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated, the landlord must send an itemized statement and return the rest of the security; receipts are not required if repair and cleaning deductions total $125 or less. A landlord who keeps security in bad faith may owe up to twice the amount of the security (Civil Code 1950.5(h), (m)).

value: The landlord must offer the tenant an initial inspection before move-out (no earlier than two weeks before the end) and must photograph the unit at the start of tenancies beginning on or after 1 July 2025 and after move-out (Civil Code 1950.5(f), (g)).

value: For non-rent-stabilized dwelling units, no deposit or advance may exceed one month's rent (with exceptions for seasonal units and owner-occupied cooperative apartments) (General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(a)).

value: Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated, the landlord must give an itemized statement of any amount kept and return the remainder; the deposit may be kept only for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid utilities payable to the landlord, and moving and storage of belongings (General Obligations Law 7-108(1-a)(b), (e)).

field: New York: notice of rent increase or non-renewal
value: If a landlord will renew with a rent increase of 5 percent or more, or will not renew, written notice is required: 30 days if the tenant has occupied under one year and has no lease of a year or more, 60 days for one to two years, 90 days for more than two years or a lease of two years or more. Late notice extends the tenancy on the existing terms until the period ends (Real Property Law 226-c).

value: A landlord may charge a late fee only if the written lease says so, the fee is reasonable, and rent has stayed unpaid two full days after the due date. A fee is presumed reasonable up to 12 percent of the rent for buildings with up to four units, or 10 percent for buildings with more than four units (Property Code 92.019).

value: After proper repair notices for conditions that affect health or safety, a tenant may have the repair made and deduct the cost from rent, up to the greater of one month's rent or $500; seven days is presumed a reasonable time to repair (Property Code 92.056(d), 92.0561).

field: Texas: lock change for unpaid rent
value: A landlord may change the locks for unpaid rent only if the lease allows it, with a written notice mailed by the fifth day or hand-delivered or posted at least three days before; the tenant must be given a key at any hour without paying (Property Code 92.0081).

value: A landlord must hold deposits and advance rent in a separate Florida account (non-interest-bearing, or interest-bearing with the tenant receiving at least 75 percent of the average annualized rate or 5 percent simple interest) or post a surety bond, and must tell the tenant in writing where it is held within 30 days (Section 83.49(1), (2)). The section reads sets no cap on the amount of a deposit.

value: If the landlord will not claim any of the deposit, it must be returned within 15 days after the tenancy ends; to claim it, the landlord must send written notice by certified mail or e-mail within 30 days, and the tenant has 15 days to object; a landlord who misses the 30 days forfeits the right to set the claim off against the deposit (Section 83.49(3)).

value: Unless the written lease says otherwise, a tenant who vacates before the end of the term, or from a periodic tenancy, must give at least 7 days' written notice by certified mail or personal delivery with a forwarding address; without it the landlord is relieved of the 15-day notice duty but the tenant keeps the right to the deposit (Section 83.49(5)).

value: A landlord may not raise rent in the first 12 months of a tenancy, and in any 12 months by more than 7 percent plus the Seattle-area consumer price index change or 10 percent, whichever is less; rent can be reset after the tenant leaves. The Department of Commerce publishes the yearly maximum. The provision expires 1 July 2040, and exemptions apply (RCW 59.18.700).
source_publisher: Washington State Legislature, Revised Code of Washington

value: A landlord must give at least 90 days' prior written notice of a rent increase, and the increase cannot take effect before the end of the rental agreement term; subsidised tenancies with income-based rent need only 30 days (RCW 59.18.140(3)).

value: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant has left (or 30 days after the landlord learns of abandonment), the landlord must give a full and specific statement of why any deposit is kept, with estimates or invoices, together with any refund due (RCW 59.18.280).

value: A landlord may demand unpaid rent in writing and state that the lease will be terminated unless the rent is paid within a stated time of at least five days after service; if not paid, the landlord may treat the lease as ended and begin an eviction action without further notice (735 ILCS 5/9-209).

value: A landlord may withhold part of a deposit for damage only if, within 30 days after the tenant vacated, it gives an itemized statement of damage with estimated or actual repair costs and paid receipts; if estimates are given, receipts follow within 30 days (765 ILCS 710/1(a)).
